column1: # Reviewed metabolite-identity corrections for MediaDB. This file is the ONLY
# place a component may be given evidence_tier "curated_mapping": a row here
# records a human decision together with the chemistry that justifies it, so a
# rebuild reproduces the correction instead of a curator re-patching data.
# Every row must carry a non-empty `chemistry` justification or the stage aborts.
#   correction_id       stable id, cited in the change ledger
#   applies_to_method   regex over the component's mapping_method; '*' = any
#   match_value         value for match_field. Regexes are CASE-SENSITIVE, because
#                       case is load-bearing chemistry here (CO2 vs Co2+).
#   current_bigg        only match components currently on this BiGG id ('' = any)
#   evidence_tier       tier to record on the corrected component
#   proxy_for           pipe-separated ids the target stands in for (class/aggregate)
#   source_name         true source string to restore when the pipeline destroyed it
#   chemistry           REQUIRED. why this is right, in chemical terms
#   reference           where the chemistry comes from
#   flux_consequential  yes|no  -- does this change what a model can take up
#   breaking_id_change  yes|no  -- does an exchange id visible to users change

column11: chemistry

Carbon dioxide is CO2 (formula CO2, InChIKey CURLTUGMZLYLDI-UHFFFAOYSA-N). cobalt2 is the cobalt(II) cation (formula Co, InChIKey XLJKHNWPARRRJB-UHFFFAOYSA-N). The two collided because BiGG's display name for cobalt2 is "Co2+", which lower-cases to the same key as "CO2"; the element sets are disjoint (C,O vs Co). Restricted to components already on cobalt2 whose name carries a carbon-dioxide/carbonate token, so the 12,009 genuine Co2+ rows are untouched.

Dietary and medium chromium is Cr(III). cro4 is chromate, CrO4, i.e. Cr(VI) -- a different oxidation state and a toxic oxyanion with dedicated reductase reactions in several GEMs. tools/bigg_metabolite_dict.json contains no Cr(III) species, so there is no correct target and the honest result is no mapping. The alias entries that produced it have been removed from tools/map_metabolite.py.
column12: audit MAP-05 verification section A; dict scan for chromium species returns only cro4

column11: cbl1 is Cob(I)alamin, the transient reduced Co(I) intracellular redox state of the cofactor -- it is not a dietary or medium B12 species. Cyanocobalamin (C63H88CoN14O14P) has no in_biggr BiGG id (b12 carries no formula and no InChIKey and is absent from BiGGr). adocbl (Adenosylcobalamin, C72H100CoN18O17P, ZIHHMGTYZOSFRC-QRVZQHAISA-N) is a real dietary/coenzyme B12 form present in BiGGr and is recorded as a declared proxy for the vitamer group, not as an exact identity.
column12: audit MAP-05(e), MAP-12 verification item 5; dict entries cbl1 / adocbl / b12

column11: b12 ("Vitamin B12") carries no formula and no InChIKey and is absent from the BiGGr reactome, so it is an unusable exchange. Harmonised onto adocbl so one analyte does not occupy two ids across the resource (184 components were on b12 while 8,145 were on cbl1 for the same nutrient).

USDA nutrient 1216 "Cystine" is L-cystine, the disulfide DIMER (C6H12N2O4S2, InChIKey LEVWYRKDKASIDU-IMJSIDKUSA-N, BiGG id cysi__L). It was mapped to cys__L, L-cysteine, the MONOMER (C3H7NO2S, XUJNEKJLAYXESH-REOHCLBHSA-N) -- a different skeleton and 2x stoichiometry -- and stamped "exact". The two USDA nutrients "Cystine" and "Cysteine" additionally collide on the same exchange key, so one measured amount silently overwrote the other. The source nutrient name was destroyed at build time (the record stores the BiGG name), so which of the two produced any given row is UNRECOVERABLE from the shipped data: the row cannot be retargeted, only relabelled and flagged. Correct target for future builds is cysi__L; see tools/curation/usda_nutrient_table.tsv.
column12: audit MAP-05(h), COV-01 verification; dict entries cys__L / cysi__L

column11: USDA "Selenium, Se" is a TOTAL ELEMENTAL selenium assay. slnt is selenite, O3Se -- one specific oxyanion. Dietary selenium is predominantly selenomethionine and selenocysteine, not the selenite ion, and selenite has dedicated reductase and sulfur-assimilation routes in many GEMs. The element measurement cannot certify an oxidation state, so this is recorded as a declared species proxy, never as an exact identity. FLUX WARNING for the bounds workstream: 6,468 food media open EX_slnt_e at lower_bound -1000 on the strength of a total-Se number, and selenite is not otherwise supplied by the injected mineral base.
column12: audit MAP-05(a) and its verification (item C: slnt and mobd are the only flux-consequential MINMAP entries)

column11: USDA "Molybdenum, Mo" is a total elemental assay; mobd is molybdate, the specific oxyanion. Same class of substitution as selenium: an element measurement does not certify a species. Flux-consequential because molybdate is not supplied by the injected mineral base.

USDA "Iron, Fe" is total iron: mixed heme and non-heme, mixed oxidation state. fe2 fixes it at Fe(II), and its BiGG display name is literally "Fe2+ mitochondria" -- a compartment-tagged name used here as an extracellular exchange. Recorded as a declared oxidation-state proxy. Not flux-consequential: the injected mineral base already opens EX_fe2_e and EX_fe3_e at -1000 in all 7,424 USDA media, so the assignment changes no bound.
column12: audit MAP-05(d) and its verification item C

column11: USDA "Phosphorus, P" is total phosphorus: phytate, phospholipid and protein-bound P as well as free orthophosphate. pi is orthophosphate alone. Recorded as a declared aggregate proxy. Not flux-consequential: EX_pi_e is already open at -1000 in every USDA medium from the injected mineral base.
column12: audit MAP-05(c) and its verification item C

column11: USDA "Vitamin B-6" reports the TOTAL of the B6 vitamer group -- pyridoxine, pyridoxal, pyridoxamine and their 5'-phosphates. pydxn is pyridoxine alone; pydx (pyridoxal) and pydam (pyridoxamine) exist separately in the dictionary. One vitamer standing for the group is a proxy and must be labelled as one.
column12: audit MAP-05(f); dict entries pydxn / pydx / pydam

column11: USDA "Folate, total" aggregates food folates (largely polyglutamyl 5-methyltetrahydrofolate) with added folic acid. fol is the folate monoglutamate; 5mthf and thf exist separately in the dictionary. Declared aggregate proxy.
column12: audit MAP-05(E); dict entries fol / 5mthf / thf

column11: USDA "Choline, total" aggregates free choline, phosphocholine, glycerophosphocholine, phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin. chol is free choline alone. Declared aggregate proxy.
USDA "Vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol)" names one tocopherol, but the assay in most records is reported as alpha-tocopherol equivalents spanning the tocopherol/tocotrienol series. Declared vitamer proxy.
column12: USDA FoodData Central nutrient definitions; dict entries avite1 / avite2

column11: MUFA 18:1 is a chain-length:unsaturation CLASS covering every C18:1 positional and geometric isomer. It was collapsed onto ocdcea (oleate, 9Z) and stamped exact. BiGG resolves six distinct C18:1 species, so the ambiguity is real and the collapse must be declared.
column12: audit MAP-08 verification (the silent half); dict scan for C18:1 species

column11: PUFA 20:4 is a class covering all C20:4 isomers; arachd is arachidonic acid (5Z,8Z,11Z,14Z) specifically. Declared class proxy.

PUFA 18:2 c declares chain length and cis geometry but not double-bond position; lnlc is linoleate (9Z,12Z) specifically. NOTE: the only alternative C18:2 id in the dictionary, ocdcya, carries the SAME InChIKey as lnlc and is a duplicate, not a class-level target -- so lnlc stays and is declared a proxy. The fully specified sibling "PUFA 18:2 n-6 c,c" is unambiguous and is deliberately NOT demoted.

PUFA 18:3 c declares chain length and cis geometry but not position; lnlnca is alpha-linolenate (9Z,12Z,15Z). The fully specified sibling "PUFA 18:3 n-3 c,c,c (ALA)" is unambiguous and is deliberately NOT demoted.
MUFA 16:1 aggregates every C16:1 isomer; hdcea is palmitoleate (9Z). The stored xref asserts the 9Z structure (InChIKey SECPZKHBENQXJG-FPLPWBNLSA-M) against a class name.
MUFA 14:1 aggregates every C14:1 isomer; ttdcea is myristoleate (9Z).
MUFA 20:1 aggregates every C20:1 isomer; M01235 is gondoate/gadoleate specifically.

MUFA 17:1 aggregates every C17:1 isomer. FLAG: hepedecacid carries no InChIKey and no formula in tools/bigg_metabolite_dict.json AND is absent from the BiGGr reactome, so this exchange asserts a metabolite whose structure the resource cannot state. Escalated for chemistry resolution or removal.
column12: audit MAP-08 verification (3,212 chemistry-free class targets)

column11: FLAG: behen carries no InChIKey and no formula in the dictionary. The chain length is unambiguous, but the resource cannot state the structure it is asserting.
MUFA 22:1 aggregates every C22:1 isomer; doco13ac is erucate (13Z).
MUFA 24:1 aggregates every C24:1 isomer; nrvnc is nervonate (15Z).

Yeast extract is an undefined mixture of amino acids, peptides, nucleotides, vitamins and salts whose composition varies by manufacturer and lot. No single BiGG exchange represents it. It is representable only as a declared decomposition into constituents (mapping_method complex_decomposition), which is a derived approximation and is labelled as one.
column12: operator decision: invented components are segregated and labelled, never presented as observations

column11: Peptones and tryptones are undefined enzymatic protein hydrolysates. No single BiGG exchange represents one. This rule also removes a specific chemistry error: "Proteose peptone (No. 3)" normalised to the key "no3" and was mapped to EX_no3_e, giving an undefined hydrolysate a nitrate uptake bound in a medium containing no nitrate.

Casein hydrolysate / casamino acids is an undefined acid or enzymatic hydrolysate of casein. Its amino-acid profile is manufacturer-specific and tryptophan is destroyed by acid hydrolysis, so a fixed expansion is an approximation, not a composition.

column4: ^\s*(?i:beef extract|meat extract|malt extract|corn steep (?:liquor|solids)|lab[- ]lemco|liver extract|brain heart infusion)\s*$
column11: Undefined biological extracts. No single BiGG exchange represents one.

A named multi-compound stock solution is not one metabolite. Wolfe's mineral solution (14 salts) had been collapsed onto molybdate alone; a Wolin/DSM-141 vitamin solution (10 vitamins) onto folate alone; a nine-vitamin string onto pyridoxine alone. The generating code (tools/enrich_coverage.py recover(), which returns on the FIRST token that maps and discards the rest) silently deleted every remaining constituent. A stock solution must be expanded into its constituents as a declared approximation, or left unmapped -- never reduced to whichever member matched first. The pattern is ANCHORED at the start of the name: a component named for ONE ion that merely annotates which stock it came from ("Copper (trace element solution)", "Biotin (Wolfe's vitamins)") is a correctly decomposed constituent and must be left alone -- an unanchored pattern deleted ~50 such rows in testing.
column12: audit MAP-10 and its verification (mechanism located at enrich_coverage.py:319-322 and :356-364)

column11: A drop-out medium's name states which nutrients are ABSENT. The pipeline split the list and supplied the first compound it could map, so four PMC6659692 media each ship exactly the one amino acid the experiment removed, at a negative uptake bound. A stated absence must never become a present component; these rows are removed from the composition and the medium is flagged for reconstruction from the paper.
column12: audit MAP-10 verification (double inversion in complexlit_PMC6659692_*)

column11: A comma-separated list of several named compounds followed by a curator gloss ("genuine cabbage flavonoids") is a mixture, not a metabolite. These strings had been collapsed onto whichever member matched first (quercetin).

co is carbon monoxide (formula CO, InChIKey UGFAIRIUMAVXCW-UHFFFAOYSA-N). Components named for cobalt chloride or cobalt sulfate are the cobalt(II) cation (formula Co, XLJKHNWPARRRJB-UHFFFAOYSA-N). Same case-folding collision as CHEM-CO2-01, in the other direction: 'Co' and 'CO' are one key once case is discarded. Restricted to components already on co whose name carries a cobalt token, so the 25 genuine carbon-monoxide rows are untouched.
column12: audit MAP-01 mechanism, extended; dict entries co / cobalt2

column11: The USDA "Vitamin B-12" nutrient rows carry the component name "Cob(I)alamin" because the builder wrote the BiGG display name over the source nutrient string, so they are invisible to a name-based rule and are matched on method plus id instead. Same chemistry as CHEM-B12-01: Cob(I)alamin is a transient reduced Co(I) intracellular redox state and is not a dietary B12 species. Deliberately scoped to usda_nutrient, so the 2,416 cbl1 rows that were INVENTED by hydrolysate_approximation and complex_decomposition are not retargeted -- changing the identity of a fabricated component would dress up a fabrication as a correction.

USDA reaches ocdcea only through the class strings "MUFA 18:1 c" and "MUFA 18:1", both of which name a chain-length:unsaturation CLASS covering every C18:1 positional and geometric isomer. The builder replaced the class string with the BiGG display name "Octadecenoate (n-C18:1)", so the rows are invisible to a name-based rule and are matched on method plus id. BiGG resolves six distinct C18:1 species, so the collapse onto oleate is a declared assumption. The two source nutrients also collide on this one exchange, so one measured amount silently overwrote the other.

USDA reaches arachd only through "PUFA 20:4" and "PUFA 20:4c", class strings covering all C20:4 isomers; arachd is arachidonate (5Z,8Z,11Z,14Z) specifically. Matched on method plus id because the class string was overwritten with the BiGG display name. The two nutrients also collide on this exchange.

USDA reaches lnlc through two nutrients: "PUFA 18:2 n-6 c,c", which is fully specified and would be exact, and "PUFA 18:2 c", which states only chain length and cis geometry. They collide on one exchange and the source string was overwritten, so which nutrient produced any given row is unrecoverable. Recorded at the FLOOR of the two, class_proxy, rather than claiming the stronger of them.
As CLASS-USDA-182: a fully specified nutrient and a class nutrient collide on one exchange and the source string was destroyed, so the row is recorded at the floor of the two.

Exception to CHEM-B12-01. Where the SOURCE itself names Cob(I)alamin, cbl1 is the right target and must not be swept into the dietary-B12 proxy. Scoped away from usda_* because the USDA rows carry "Cob(I)alamin" only as an echo of the BiGG display name the builder wrote over the source nutrient string -- there the name is the pipeline's word, not the source's.

A bare "PUFA 18:2" states chain length and degree of unsaturation only -- no double-bond position, no geometry -- so it covers every C18:2 isomer. lnlc is linoleate (9Z,12Z). The fully specified "PUFA 18:2 n-6 c,c" is excluded by the negative lookahead and stays at its name tier, because there the source string does fix the compound.
As CLASS-FA-182B: a bare "PUFA 18:3" covers every C18:3 isomer; lnlnca is alpha-linolenate (9Z,12Z,15Z). "PUFA 18:3 n-3 c,c,c (ALA)" is excluded and keeps its name tier.
A bare "PUFA 20:3" covers every C20:3 isomer; dlnlcg is dihomo-gamma-linolenate (8Z,11Z,14Z) specifically.
A bare "PUFA 20:2" covers every C20:2 isomer; M00008 is 11Z,14Z-eicosadienoate specifically.

Vitamin A, IU and "Vitamin A, RAE" are ACTIVITY aggregates: they sum preformed retinol and the provitamin A carotenoids (beta-carotene, alpha-carotene, beta-cryptoxanthin) after applying conversion factors. Mapping the aggregate onto retinol alone assigns one member of the group the whole activity, and a bacterium cannot convert IU into a molar uptake. Declared aggregate proxy. The separately reported "Retinol" nutrient is a specific compound and is deliberately NOT matched by this pattern.

column4: ^Vitamin D \(D2 \+ D3\)|^Vitamin D2\+D3|^Vitamin D, IU|^Vitamin D$
column11: Vitamin D (D2 + D3) explicitly sums two distinct compounds -- ergocalciferol (D2) and cholecalciferol (D3) -- and is reported in International Units. vitd3 is cholecalciferol alone. Declared aggregate proxy.

C18:3 n-6 is GAMMA-linolenic acid (lnlncg, C18H29O2, InChIKey VZCCETWTMQHEPK-QNEBEIHSSA-M, in BiGGr). It had been mapped to lnlnca, ALPHA-linolenic acid, which is C18:3 n-3 -- the same chain length and degree of unsaturation but different double-bond positions, so a different compound with a different InChIKey (DTOSIQBPPRVQHS-PDBXOOCHSA-M). The n-3/n-6 distinction is the whole point of reporting these separately. Also corrected in the mapper alias table.
column12: dict entries lnlnca / lnlncg; found by hand-verifying the class_proxy stratum of this pass

column11: cystine__L carries no formula, no InChIKey and is absent from the BiGGr reactome, so EX_cystine__L_e is an unusable exchange. cysi__L is L-cystine proper: C6H12N2O4S2, InChIKey LEVWYRKDKASIDU-IMJSIDKUSA-N, in_biggr true. These 527 rows keep their source name, so unlike the USDA cys__L rows (CHEM-CYS-01) they CAN be retargeted rather than only relabelled. Harmonises the resource onto one id for one analyte.
column12: dict entries cystine__L / cysi__L; audit COV-01 verification item 2

column11: Companion to CHEM-GLA-01 for the rows that landed on dlnlcg instead of lnlnca. Gamma-linolenic acid is C18:3 n-6 (lnlncg, C18H29O2). dlnlcg is DIHOMO-gamma-linolenic acid, C20:3 n-6 (C20H33O2) -- two carbons longer, a different metabolite with a different InChIKey. The negative lookahead protects the rows where the source genuinely says dihomo, and "PUFA 20:3" / "PUFA 20:3 n-6" are untouched because they do not match the name pattern.
column12: dict entries lnlncg / dlnlcg; found in the review queue of this pass
